newsitem.title: USA: Early crop-killing freeze entering U.S. Midwest.
newsitem.headline: Early crop-killing freeze entering U.S. Midwest.

text.p: A crop-killing freeze entered the western U.S. Midwest early Wednesday and should spread Thursday and early Friday across Iowa, northern Illinois, northern Indiana and northwest Ohio, meteorologists said.
The freezing weather will be seven to 14 days earlier than normal for many areas of the Midwest.
"That should effectively end the growing season in the northern part of the belt," said Joel Burgio, meteorologist with Weather Services Corp.

Low temperatures early Thursday morning may range from the mid to upper 20s degrees Fahrenheit across South Dakota, Minnesota, northern Iowa and Wisconsin. Lows from the upper 20s to low 30s were forecast for southern Iowa, northern Missouri, and northwest Illinois.
Friday morning lows may range from the high 20s to mid 30s in central Illinois, central Indiana and central Ohio.

Fred Gesser, meteorologist with Weather Express Inc, said high temperatures during this period will be in the 60s. However, a rapid warmup is forecast begin Friday through the weekend when high temperatures should be in the 70s.
Much of the Midwest and Great Plains should be dry through the weekend, which may allow harvesting of corn and soybeans and planting of winter wheat, the meteorologists said.

However, in areas where fields are wet, Burgio and Gesser said, it is unlikely the freezing weather will harden the ground long enough to allow for significant harvesting. The warming trend beginning Friday will put low temperatures across the Midwest in the 40s and highs in the 70s through the weekend.
In the Plains, mostly rain-free days were forecast until early next week which should allow rapid planting of hard red winter wheat, said Weather Services' Burgio.
